closed_instance_rule_size.theorem: For any satisfiable closed SAT instance F(x_1,...,x_n), there exists a zero-input Skolem rule vector of size O(n): the constant bits of any satisfying assignment.
closed_instance_rule_size.meaning: Polynomial Skolem-rule size is not the hard part for closed SAT; finding the constants is exactly witness search.
closed_instance_rule_size.unsat_side: For UNSAT there is no SAT witness to reconstruct, so terminalization must instead supply a complete exact UNSAT certificate.

uniform_synthesis_barrier.theorem: A deterministic polynomial-time procedure that, for every closed Boolean relation F(X), synthesizes a valid zero-input Skolem vector f() whenever F is satisfiable decides SAT in polynomial time: evaluate F(f()); validity forces TRUE exactly on satisfiable F.
uniform_synthesis_barrier.consequence: Universal polynomial-time debt discharge by Skolem synthesis is already solver-equivalent on closed instances; the debt ledger does not by itself reduce the universal hardness obligation.
uniform_synthesis_barrier.claim_ceiling: This is an equivalence/barrier statement, not a proof that such synthesis cannot exist.

generic_rule_validation.problem: SKOLEM_VALID(R,f): for all y, ((exists x R(x,y)) -> R(f(y),y))
generic_rule_validation.membership: coNP, because invalidity has polynomial witness (y,x) with R(x,y)=1 and R(f(y),y)=0.
generic_rule_validation.hardness_reduction: Given 3CNF G(y), define the polynomial-size Boolean DAG R_G(x,y)=x OR NOT G(y) and fixed rule f(y)=0. Then exists x R_G(x,y) is always true, while R_G(0,y)=NOT G(y). Therefore f is valid iff G is UNSAT.
generic_rule_validation.representation_binding: R_G is a polynomial-size bounded-fanin Boolean DAG and may be Tseitin-compiled with polynomial overhead to 3CNF and then to PAIR+OR_3 under the existing exact selector compiler.
implications: A generic deterministic polynomial-time raw validity checker would imply P=NP.
Polynomial-size independently checkable certificates for every valid generic rule would imply NP=coNP.
Therefore U-PAIR-1I may not assume generic rule validation is easy; any admissible discharge must carry a restricted structured proof whose polynomial size is itself proved.

positive_controls.affine_pivot: linear GF(2) rule obtained from RREF
positive_controls.single_OR_control: constant satisfying selection when its precondition is locally certified

result.main_lesson: Existential-debt bookkeeping blocks fake progress, but a universal Skolem discharge step hides the original search problem in synthesis and a coNP-complete obligation in generic validation. The next candidate must freeze a proof-carrying discharge calculus whose local verification is polynomial and whose proof/synthesis size is globally bounded by a polynomial.

survives: structured locally certified Skolem rules for tractable subcases
a future proof-carrying Skolem synthesis calculus with a proved polynomial proof-size and synthesis bound
